name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Grijalva with large fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Grijalva: a D+13 district, incumbency, and a dominant money edge — she has raised roughly ten times her opponent, who had under $12,000 on hand. Markets price her win at about 95%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A surprise surge of outside spending against Grijalva or unusually low special-election turnout could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to flip the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Adelita Grijalva, the Democratic incumbent in this heavily Democratic southern Arizona district, is seeking her first full term after winning the seat in a special election. The district's partisan lean of D+13 gives her a substantial structural advantage, and she carries the Grijalva family name long associated with the seat.

Her Republican challenger, Daniel Butierez, has run a low-budget campaign, raising about $224,000 with minimal cash remaining, while Grijalva has raised over $2.2 million. No independent polls of the race are available, but prediction markets put her chances near 95%. The evidence supports a Safe D rating, with the main uncertainty being turnout in a low-profile contest.
